newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes see slight gains with WTI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes see slight gains with WTI.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices edged up with West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Friday, while trade for Alaskan crude idled as refiners squared their positions for March.
BP America, a key producer of the grade, offered Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude at $1.25 below March NYMEX and said bidders were as wide as $1.50 a barrel under.

Traders failed to agree on which basis to use for ANS deals, with NYMEX February crude rolling into the cheaper March contract earlier this week, and thin spot February barrels seen as an unreliable benchmark by regional buyers.
Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude rose 15 cents to $22.37/22.57 a barrel, in line with WTI increases.
The postings market for Line 63 crude was flat, after a deal got done at $1.00 over Buena Vista earlier this week.
No deals were reported for Line 63 on a fixed basis, but one trader claimed the discount stood about $2.20 to $2.30 below WTI.
Meanwhile, the market for California heavy crudes was talked lower than early week levels, with players hearing trades at 25 to 50 cents below the postings.

Wilmington was heard done at 95 cents over postings earlier this week, a sharp increase over recent range of 40 to cents over postings. Traders cited falling production at the Long Beach-area oil field.
